main_method.title: GRU-ODE-Bayes: Continuous modeling of sporadically-observed time series
main_method.supplement_limit: Official supplemental click returned an internal tool error; appendix-only proofs were not verified.

method_evidence.claim: A newly observed dimension can update predictions of a correlated unobserved dimension.
Continuous GRU hidden-state evolution with masked discrete observation jumps and pre/post losses.
Paper post loss uses KL(p_Bayes || p_post), with p_Bayes proportional to pre and observation distributions.
Future values are obtained by continuous propagation to a calendar query time; future-event-index prediction is not automatically the same estimand.

core_source_read_ranges.level: Read main cells, NNFOwithBayesianJumps, loss and solver code; subsequent alternatives not fully audited.
Read dataset slicing, collation, validation-time organization and extraction; indexed remaining function names only.

static_findings.finding: Main author code computes KL(p_post || N(observation,0.01^2)), not the paper's full-posterior KL direction.
Unpinned dependencies, deprecated NumPy aliases, and a separate modified torchdiffeq install; no compatibility claim or install performed.

static_findings.where: models.py ode_step and forward; data_utils.py extract_from_path
static_findings.finding: Fixed Euler steps may overshoot an off-grid observation time; extraction can map a query to the closest stored time. This is a static numerical-interface issue, not a demonstrated empirical leak.
For fixed finite weights, a continuous decoder over the bounded hidden state has bounded mean output. This is an own mathematical observation, not a carbon performance result.
